Hi Liam,

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and the agreed next steps:

- Deployment preference: Private VPC (FintechCo needs customer-managed VPC with PrivateLink or VPC peering).
- Key networking asks: support for AWS PrivateLink (VPC endpoint), option for VPC peering if preferred, and static IP allowlist for outbound traffic to integrate with third-party IP allowlists.
- Security/Compliance: SOC 2 report requested - I'll attach a current snapshot and our Private deployment guide for your infra/security team.
- Timeline: Proof-of-concept targeted for early September; procurement reviewing contract terms next week.

Next steps:
1) Please send the network contact and a brief current VPC layout (CIDR, whether you prefer PrivateLink vs peering).
2) I'll loop in Sean (solutions eng) for a short technical call to confirm routing and NAT/egress requirements.
3) I'll upload the docs mentioned and your team can flag any further evidence requests.

Attachments: fintechco_vpc_requirements.xlsx (your worksheet), redwood-private-deployment-guide.pdf, SOC2-snapshot.pdf

Best,

Hi Amit - thanks for the diagram.

Quick notes ahead of the call:
- PrivateLink is generally our preferred customer-facing option (no inbound routing changes required on your side). We create a VPC endpoint service in our account and you create an endpoint in yours.
- For egress to third-party services, customers typically request one of the following: 1) Redwood publishes a set of static egress IPs (we can provide a list and maintain it), or 2) traffic egresses via your NAT/egress and we accept inbound via PrivateLink (we can support both patterns).
- Port requirements: 443 for API traffic; we may also need 5432/3306 if we set up any inbound DB-like integrations (rare - we'll avoid when possible).
- We'll send a short checklist before the call: VPC CIDRs, route table entries for endpoints, SG rules to allow PrivateLink, and whether you require mutual TLS.

If PrivateLink works for you, please confirm and we'll proceed with a short provisioning checklist and schedule the POC window.

Cheers,
